points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 威廉·哈维于1578年4月1日出生于英国肯特郡福克斯通的一个富裕家庭。他在当地接受了基础教育后，进入坎特伯雷国王学校学习。在这里，他展现了卓越的学术才能，特别是在古典文学和自然科学方面。这段早期教育为他后来的医学研究奠定了坚实基础，培养了他对自然现象的观察力和分析能力。哈维的家庭支持他接受高等教育，这为他进入剑桥大学创造了条件。
points.descriptionEn: William Harvey was born on April 1, 1578, in Folkestone, Kent, England, into a wealthy family. After receiving basic education locally, he attended the King's School in Canterbury, where he demonstrated exceptional academic abilities, particularly in classical literature and natural sciences. This early education laid a solid foundation for his later medical research, developing his observational and analytical skills. Harvey's family supported his higher education, which enabled him to proceed to Cambridge University.

points.title: 剑桥求学
points.description: 哈维进入剑桥大学冈维尔-凯厄斯学院学习，主修艺术和医学。在剑桥期间，他深受亚里士多德和盖伦等古代医学思想家的影响，同时也开始质疑盖伦学说的某些观点。1600年，他前往欧洲大陆继续深造，在帕多瓦大学跟随著名解剖学家法布里修斯学习。帕多瓦大学是当时欧洲领先的医学研究中心，哈维在这里接受了严格的解剖学训练，并开始形成自己关于血液循环的初步想法。
points.descriptionEn: Harvey entered Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge University, where he studied arts and medicine. During his time at Cambridge, he was influenced by ancient medical thinkers like Aristotle and Galen, but also began to question certain aspects of Galenic doctrine. In 1600, he traveled to continental Europe to further his studies, studying under the renowned anatomist Fabricius at the University of Padua. Padua was then Europe's leading medical research center, where Harvey received rigorous anatomical training and began forming his initial ideas about blood circulation.

points.title: 皇家医师
points.description: 1602年，哈维获得剑桥大学医学学位后返回伦敦，成为圣巴多罗买医院的医师。1618年，他被任命为詹姆斯一世的御医，后来又成为查理一世的御医。在伦敦期间，哈维进行了大量的解剖学研究，特别是在动物活体实验方面。他通过解剖多种动物，观察心脏和血管的工作方式，逐渐形成了血液循环理论。这一时期，他积累了大量实验证据，为日后发表革命性的医学理论奠定了基础。哈维在宫廷中的地位使他能够获得研究资源和时间，但也使他后来在英国内战期间陷入困境。
points.descriptionEn: After receiving his medical degree from Cambridge in 1602, Harvey returned to London and became a physician at St. Bartholomew's Hospital. In 1618, he was appointed physician to James I and later became physician to Charles I. During his time in London, Harvey conducted extensive anatomical research, particularly in animal vivisection. By dissecting various animals and observing how the heart and blood vessels functioned, he gradually developed his theory of blood circulation. During this period, he accumulated extensive experimental evidence that laid the foundation for his later revolutionary medical theories. Harvey's position at court provided him with research resources and time, but also placed him in difficulties during the English Civil War.

points.title: 血液循环理论发表
points.description: 1628年，哈维出版了《心血运动论》(De Motu Cordis)，这是医学史上最具革命性的著作之一。在这本书中，他通过详细的解剖学观察和实验，证明了血液在体内循环流动，而非像盖伦学说认为的那样是由肝脏产生并被身体消耗。哈维计算出心脏每次搏动泵出的血量，并据此推断血液必须在体内循环。这一理论彻底改变了人们对人体生理功能的理解，为现代生理学奠定了基础。尽管最初遭到许多医学界同行的反对，但哈维的理论逐渐被接受，并成为现代医学的基石。查理一世对哈维的研究给予大力支持，甚至在宫廷中安排活体解剖演示。
points.descriptionEn: In 1628, Harvey published 'De Motu Cordis' (On the Motion of the Heart and Blood), one of the most revolutionary works in medical history. In this book, through detailed anatomical observations and experiments, he demonstrated that blood circulates throughout the body rather than being produced by the liver and consumed by the body as Galenic doctrine claimed. Harvey calculated the amount of blood pumped by the heart with each beat and inferred that blood must circulate within the body. This theory completely changed the understanding of human physiological functions and laid the foundation for modern physiology. Although initially opposed by many medical colleagues, Harvey's theory gradually gained acceptance and became a cornerstone of modern medicine. Charles I strongly supported Harvey's research, even arranging vivisections at court.

points.title: 晚年研究与遗产
points.description: 英国内战爆发后，哈维因支持查理一世而失去了御医职位和大部分财产。他隐退到伦敦郊区，继续研究动物生殖和胚胎发育。1651年，他出版了《动物生殖论》(Exercitationes de Generatione Animalium)，详细研究了胚胎发育过程。哈晚年的研究虽然不如血液循环理论那样具有革命性，但仍为胚胎学做出了重要贡献。1657年，哈维在伦敦去世，被安葬在汉普斯特德圣安德鲁教堂。他的血液循环理论最终被医学界完全接受，彻底改变了医学实践，为现代生理学和医学研究奠定了基础。哈维被视为现代实验医学的奠基人之一，他的研究方法强调观察和实验，而非盲从古代权威。
points.descriptionEn: After the outbreak of the English Civil War, Harvey lost his position as court physician and most of his property due to his support for Charles I. He retired to the outskirts of London, where he continued to study animal reproduction and embryonic development. In 1651, he published 'Exercitationes de Generatione Animalium' (On the Generation of Animals), detailing the process of embryonic development. Although Harvey's later research was not as revolutionary as his theory of circulation, it still made important contributions to embryology. Harvey died in London in 1657 and was buried in St. Andrew's Church, Hampstead. His theory of blood circulation was eventually fully accepted by the medical community, completely changing medical practice and laying the foundation for modern physiology and medical research. Harvey is regarded as one of the founders of modern experimental medicine, emphasizing observation and experimentation over blind adherence to ancient authorities.

appraisal.zh: 哈维被公认为科学革命的先驱之一，其血液循环理论通过系统实验与观察，把零散发现整合为完整体系，推动医学从古代权威转向实证科学，他倡导的实验方法更成为现代医学的象征。不过也有研究者指出，他未能解释血液如何从动脉毛细血管进入静脉毛细血管，且过度强调心脏的作用；另一种看法认为，他的贡献被过度神话化，实为在前人基础上取得突破，其宫廷身份也可能影响客观性。
appraisal.en: Harvey is widely recognized as a pioneer of the Scientific Revolution: his theory of blood circulation integrated scattered findings into a comprehensive system through systematic experiment and observation, turning medicine from ancient authority toward empirical science, and the experimental methods he championed made him a symbol of modern medicine. Yet some researchers note that he could not explain how blood passes from arterial to venous capillaries and overemphasized the heart; another view holds that his contributions have been overly mythologized, that he built on predecessors, and that his court position may have affected his objectivity.

supporter.zh: 哈维被誉为现代医学的奠基人之一，他的血液循环理论彻底改变了医学史。通过严谨的观察和实验，他推翻了统治医学界近1500年的盖伦学说，建立了基于实证的生理学基础。哈维的研究方法强调实验验证而非盲从权威，为现代科学方法树立了典范。他的工作不仅拯救了无数生命，还为后来的医学研究开辟了新道路。哈维的坚持和勇气使他能够在面对强烈反对时坚持真理，这种科学精神至今仍激励着医学研究者。
supporter.en: Harvey is hailed as one of the founders of modern medicine, whose theory of blood circulation revolutionized medical history. Through rigorous observation and experimentation, he overturned the Galenic doctrine that had dominated medicine for nearly 1,500 years, establishing an empirical foundation for physiology. Harvey's research methodology emphasized experimental verification over blind adherence to authority, setting an example for modern scientific methods. His work not only saved countless lives but also开辟 new paths for subsequent medical research. Harvey's perseverance and courage in facing strong opposition while upholding truth continue to inspire medical researchers today.

critic.zh: 批评者指出哈维的理论存在局限性，他未能解释血液如何从动脉毛细血管进入静脉毛细血管，这一问题直到显微镜发明后才得到解决。此外，哈维过度强调心脏在血液循环中的作用，相对忽视了其他器官的功能。他的研究方法虽然开创性，但有时过于简化复杂生理过程。哈维在宫廷中的地位也使他能够获得研究资源，但也可能影响了他的客观性。一些现代医学史学者认为，哈维的贡献被过度神话化，实际上他是在多位前人研究基础上取得的突破。
critic.en: Critics point out that Harvey's theory had limitations, as he failed to explain how blood moves from arterial capillaries to venous capillaries—a problem only solved after the invention of the microscope. Additionally, Harvey overemphasized the heart's role in circulation while relatively neglecting the functions of other organs. Although his research methods were pioneering, they sometimes oversimplified complex physiological processes. Harvey's position at court provided him with research resources but may have affected his objectivity. Some modern medical historians argue that Harvey's contributions have been overly mythologized, and that he actually built upon the work of several predecessors.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，哈维被公认为科学革命的先驱人物之一，他的工作标志着医学从古代权威向现代实证科学的转变。哈维的血液循环理论虽然不是完全原创，但他通过系统的实验和观察，将零散的发现整合成一个完整的理论体系。在流行文化中，哈维常被描绘为孤独的天才，面对保守势力的反对坚持真理。然而，历史研究表明，他的成功也得益于当时科学氛围的转变和前人的研究基础。哈维的遗产不仅在于他的具体发现，更在于他倡导的实验方法和科学精神，这使他成为现代医学的象征性人物。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Harvey is widely recognized as one of the pioneers of the Scientific Revolution, whose work marked medicine's transition from ancient authority to modern empirical science. Although his theory of blood circulation was not entirely original, he integrated scattered discoveries into a comprehensive theoretical system through systematic experiments and observations. In popular culture, Harvey is often depicted as a lonely genius who persisted in truth against conservative opposition. However, historical research indicates that his success also benefited from the changing scientific atmosphere and the foundation of previous research. Harvey's legacy lies not only in his specific discoveries but in the experimental methods and scientific spirit he advocated, making him a symbolic figure in modern medicine.

self.zh: 我害怕的不是无知，而是那些自以为知道一切的人。
self.en: I fear not the man who has practiced ten thousand kicks once, but I fear the man who has practiced one kick ten thousand times.
